entityDescription:
The Euro-Atlantic Resilience Centre (E-ARC) is a centre of excellence in the field of resilience, a partner of NATO and the EU, acting for the benefit of these organisations, as well as Member States or partners.
The establishment of the Centre was recognized and welcomed in the joint statement of the heads of state and government gathered on the occasion of the Brussels Summit in June 14th, 2021: „We will continue to take a whole-of-government approach to enhancing the resilience of our societies. […]We welcome the establishment of the Euro-Atlantic Centre for Resilience in Romania.”
The Centre carries out its activity in synergy with the objectives of the EU and NATO in the field of resilience, without being directly subordinated to either of these organisations. In this way, E-ARC can also offer expertise to states in the Black Sea area which are not EU or NATO members (Moldova, Ukraine, Georgia, etc.).

According to Government Decision 565 of May 19, 2021, the mission of E-ARC is to develop concepts, doctrines and methodologies in the field of resilience, to provide training courses and to offer a platform for the transfer of expertise between the government institutions, the private sector, civil society and academia. E-ARC is not a national resilience authority and does not have operational responsibilities.
Supporting NATO's efforts to create the new concept of layered resilience, E-ARC is coordinating, in partnership with the Romanian Ministry of Defence, the development of NATO doctrine on Response Planning, one of the seven thematic areas that form the Alliance's Layered Resilience strategy.
At NATO's Riga seminar in April 2023, the Centre was formally invited by Allied Command Transformation (NATO ACT) to present the Euro-Atlantic vision of societal resilience. Similarly, E-ARC is already working, in coordination with NATO, on missions to assess and support resilience in states in the Black Sea region.
Since November 2023, E-ARC has been organizing, in Bucharest, in collaboration with NATO Defence Policy & Planning Division, the Course dedicated to resilience experts, to strengthen the Organization's capacity to respond in a coordinated manner to crises that threaten the resilience of member states.
The Centre’s experts have offered training sessions, courses, and high level briefings on strengthening resilience for Romanian and foreign diplomats, as well as for government officials from EU member states and partners, for example a session in partnership with EUAM Ukraine. So far, the courses have covered topics such as institutional resilience, societal resilience, resilience of transport infrastructure and resilience of communication systems.

entityDescription:
Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Technologies and Transport Institute(MATTI) is an innovative and development-oriented educational and research institution actively operating in the field of engineering and technology. The institute prides itself on a wide range of research areas, including:
- mechanical engineering technologies
- biomedical engineering
- applied mechanics
- thermal engineering
- manufacturing automation
- nanoengineering
- powder materials technologies
- mechatronics
- tribology
- metrology
- welding technologies
- space technologies
- air transport
- land transport
- mobility technologies
- smart textiles.
MATTI scientists are actively involved in both national and international projects, making a significant contribution to the advancement of science and technology. Research results are regularly published in internationally recognized scientific journals. The institute has created several patented inventions and developed knowledge that fosters innovation.
MATTI is a place where science and technology meet practical application, creating solutions that change the world.
Scientific Competencies
MATTI's scientific activities cover several significant areas. The main research competencies include mechanical engineering, with a special focus on metrology and tribology, biomedical engineering with an emphasis on nanoengineering and smart sensors, as well as theoretical mechanics, exploring nonlinear vibrations. In addition, the institute specializes in industrial engineering, focusing on CNC machining, as well as heat and cold transfer technologies and industrial design.Scientific activities also coverdevelopment of space mission designs, research on aircraft and drone design, studies on material and component fatigue, development of autonomous control solutions, road traffic safety analysis, and research on sustainably sourced fuels.
Scientific Laboratories
MATTI includes several specialized scientific laboratories that ensure high-quality research and development work. Among them are the Biomedical and Nanoengineering Laboratory, focusing on biochip technologies and smart textiles, the Powder Materials Laboratory, the Welding and Thermal Processes Laboratory, as well as the Metrology Laboratory, which provides precise measurements and calibrations. In addition, research is conducted in the fields of mechanics, biotextile materials, machine and mechanism dynamics, and tribology in the institute's laboratories.
Research Directions
MATTI's research directions cover a wide spectrum, ranging from 3D biotextiles with nanocomposite-enhanced protective properties to experimental research and modeling of composite materials. The institute also conducts research on multifunctional nanostructured smart coatings and the micro and macro mechanical and tribological properties of surfaces. Other significant research areas include improving the efficiency of heat supply operations and replacing fossil fuels with alternative energy sources, as well as industrial design.
MATTI is a place where science and technology meet practical application, creating solutions that change the world. The institute invites both students and industry representatives to collaborate in shaping the future together.

entityDescription:
Research at the Institute of Quantum Optics focuses on highly controlled interaction of light and matter. Typical topics are the physics of ultracold quantum gases, quantum logic spectroscopy based on cooling and trapping of ions dealing with fundamental principles of physics, the physics of ultrashort laser pulses and the control of plasmas in the sub-femto region and applications of nonlinear optics in medical therapy and diagnostics. The institute also provides central parts of the education within the Bachelor and Master courses in physics and related topics.

The Institute of Quantum Optics (IQO) at Leibniz University Hannover specialises in fundamental and applied research on laser physics and light-matter interactions. It explores extremes from Bose-Einstein condensates to femtosecond/attosecond plasmas, spanning ultracold atoms, molecules, and biological systems, with extensions into quantum information and relativistic satellite experiments.​
Research Focus
Key questions drive the work: improving lasers, their applications, and insights from light-matter interactions. Efforts target precise atomic clocks/sensors, atom-molecule control, laser surgery innovations, cell manipulation, quantum computers, and X-ray lasers.​
- Internal groups: Guided Matter Wave Interferometry (Dr Schlippert), Molecular Quantum Gases (Prof Dr S Ospelkaus), Quantum Atom Optics (Prof Dr Ertmer, apl Prof Dr Klempt), Theory of Quantum Sensing (Dr Naceur Gaaloul), Quantum Sensing (Prof Dr Ertmer, Prof Dr Rasel), Trapped-Ion Quantum Engineering (Prof Dr C Ospelkaus), Ultrafast Laser Laboratory (Prof Dr Morgner et al).​

- External sites: Biophotonics (Prof Dr Heisterkamp), Nanoengineering (Prof Dr Chichkov), Laser Components and Fibres (Prof Dr Ristau), Quantum Logic Spectroscopy (Prof Dr Schmidt), Quantum Clocks and Complex Systems (Prof Dr Tanja Mehlstäubler).​

Collaborations
The institute partners locally with Laser Zentrum Hannover (LZH), PTB Braunschweig, NIFE, and DLR-SI, plus national/international institutions. Major initiatives include QUEST Leibniz Research School, Clusters of Excellence (PhoenixD, QuantumFrontiers, Hearing4all), QVLS Quantum Valley Lower Saxony, and funding from DFG, EU, ESA

Climate Resource S GmbH is a small specialist climate science software and advisory firm. It was founded in 2024 as a wholly owned subsidiary of Climate Resource Pty Ltd, to be the European arm of Climate Resource Pty Ltd. Climate Resource Pty Ltd was incorporated in 2020 in Australia. Climate Resource Pty Ltd and Climate Resource S GmbH together form the Climate Resource Group, although there is no legal entity which represents the Climate Resource Group and the two companies operate on arms’ length principles. The Climate Resource group now has staff based in Melbourne, Australia; Vienna, Austria; Berlin, Germany and Hanover, Germany. All of the European staff are employees of Climate Resource S GmbH.

The Climate Resource Group’s network of clients and collaborations has expanded rapidly to include multilateral organisations, governments, financial institutions, consulting firms, and science research organisations including the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project International Project Office (CMIP IPO) and Australia’s national science agency (CSIRO). The Climate Resource team has decades of experience in climate science and policy, particularly climate projections using reduced complexity climate models for the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) and quantification of the emissions consistent with country pledges in nationally determined contributions (NDCs) and long-term low-emissions development strategies (LT-LEDS) submitted to the UNFCCC. Multiple members of the team contributed to the IPCC’s Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) and the Scientific Director, Malte Meinshausen, has been contributing to IPCC reports since the Fourth Assessment Report (AR4). Members of the team have also been contributing greenhouse gas concentration input model forcing data to CMIP since CMIP5. In addition to their scientific credentials, the Climate Resource Group also specialises in research software engineering. The team has experience in delivering high-quality research software tools, with a particular focus on reproducibility, transparency and robustness, a key requirement for operationalisation of existing scientific workflows.

As a note: in the absence of financial statements for Climate Resource S GmbH (Climate Resource S GmbH was only established in 2024 so there are obviously no financial statements for 2023 or earlier) we have included the audited financial statements of Climate Resource Pty Ltd in Section 9.
